title: Clinical outcome and implant survival after knee TEP change to triathlon PS and TS systems
summary:
The implantation of the total knee arthroplasty (KTEP) is an established and successful procedure worldwide for knee arthrosis with exhausted conservative therapeutic measures. Frequently, more stabilizing total knee arthroplasties (KTEP) are necessary as part of the change operations in order to achieve satisfactory stability in the knee joint. An example of a frequently performed change operation is the change to a posterior stabilized prosthesis (PS) or a totally stabilized prosthesis (TS). In this study, we would first like to question all patients who were treated with the corresponding implants during a replacement operation in order to investigate the so-called implant survival and the revision rate after the replacement operation. The different types of implants should be analyzed separately.
Furthermore, patient satisfaction and the subjective function of the joint are to be examined as part of a patient survey using questionnaires. In addition, the radiological recordings that have already been carried out are to be analyzed with regard to common radiological criteria for knee arthroplasty (loosening, joint and implant position).
conditions: Presence of a knee joint prosthesis
Complications of internal orthopaedic prosthetic devices, implants and grafts

interventions.name: In this group, patients are asked about implant survival and the revision rate. You have received a total knee endoprosthesis change to the PS system (posterior stabilized prosthesis).
In this group, patients are asked about implant survival and the revision rate. You have received a total knee endoprosthesis change to the TS system (totally stabilized prosthesis).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Male or female patients aged ≥ 18 years
- Knee TEP change performed on Stryker Triathlon PS or Triathlon TS prostheses
Exclusion criteria:
- Another revision of the knee TEP with replacement of individual or all components
